evals.prompt: I've finished the retry logic in src/http/client.ts and added tests in tests/client.test.ts. Keep reviewing and fixing it with an independent reviewer until it's clean. The worktree also has unrelated WIP in src/ui/ — leave that alone.
evals.expected_output: Initialises the loop scoped to client.ts + client.test.ts only, recording the retry requirements as `--task-brief` (requirements only — not its own rationale or suspected issues), runs focused tests before the first pass, spawns a fresh sub-agent with the template prompt filled from `status` including the brief, records score/findings via the script, fixes findings as a batch, re-validates with the full set of checks the previous pass rested on (not just the quick one), repeats, and finishes with `accept` and the final report. Never touches src/ui/.

evals.prompt: Loop-review my current changes. If the reviewer scores 6/10 but lists no findings, what do you do?
evals.expected_output: Records the pass with findings=0, notes the score is calibration noise, does not open another pass on unchanged code, asks the same reviewer once for concrete findings if the summary hints at concerns, records anything it supplies with `amend` against the same pass rather than via pass-start --force, and accepts if validation is green, understanding is credible and test evidence is recorded as trusted or justifiably absent.

evals.prompt: Run /loop-code-review on the migration in db/migrations/0042_add_index.sql and the model change in app/models/order.py. It's ambiguous whether app/models/customer.py changes are mine or from the other branch I merged.
evals.expected_output: Asks the user about customer.py ownership before initialising scope rather than guessing or reviewing the whole worktree.

evals.prompt: Loop-review this until a reviewer signs off. After 5 passes there's still one finding you believe is wrong.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the finding with evidence to the same reviewer, escalates once to a fresh adjudicator, and if still unresolved reports an INCOMPLETE outcome with the exact blocker rather than forcing a sixth pass or lowering the bar.

evals.prompt: Loop-review src/parser.ts. Your first validation command was a typo (`pytset tests/`, exit 127); the corrected run of `pytest tests/` is green, but pass-start refuses to open a pass.
evals.expected_output: Retracts the mistyped record with `validate-drop -- pytset tests/` and opens the pass; does not use `pass-start --force`, does not reset the loop, and does not touch files to shift the fingerprint. Would refuse to drop a command that actually ran and failed.

evals.prompt: Run a full loop code review of this whole repository and fix what you find.
evals.expected_output: Maps areas from the repo structure (packages/apps/modules), shows the list once, runs `project init` (fix mode, or report-only if it judges cross-area ripple likely and says so), then `project next` -> normal loop with reviewer-prompt-area.md -> writes findings file -> `project close`, area after area without asking. In report-only it stops each area after recording the pass and writing the findings — no fixes, no `accept`. Closes stuck areas as incomplete and continues, and ends with the per-area ledger from `project status --json`.

evals.prompt: Loop-review my last commit (it's already on HEAD).
evals.expected_output: Hits `init` exiting 2 with `no-changes` (or anticipates it) and re-runs with `--base HEAD~1` (or the parent of the first task commit) instead of reviewing on a blind fingerprint. Does not reach for `--allow-empty`, which would give it a loop where every gate passes vacuously.

evals.prompt: Loop-review the export feature I just built in src/export/. The spec: CSV export must stream, must cap at 100k rows, and must never include the internal `_shard` column.
evals.expected_output: Records the three requirements verbatim as the task brief at `init` (--task-brief or --task-brief-file), passes them to the reviewer as `status` prints them, and treats an unmet or partially met requirement — e.g. streaming implemented but no row cap — as an actionable finding rather than a nit. Does not add its own design rationale or suspected issues to the brief.

evals.prompt: Loop-review my changes to src/auth/session.ts.
evals.expected_output: If `init` exits 2 because the scoped diff is empty, does not proceed: it checks whether the work is committed (then `--base`), whether the path is wrong (then fixes it), and otherwise reports the outcome `no-changes` and stops. Never uses `--allow-empty` on its own initiative to get a loop started.

evals.prompt: Loop-review this. The reviewer's one finding looks wrong to you; you escalated to an adjudicator and its verdict is two vague sentences that neither uphold nor invalidate the finding.
evals.expected_output: Asks the adjudicator once for the missing reasoning. If the verdict is still unusable, leaves the finding unresolved and reports INCOMPLETE with it as the blocker — it does not record `resolve --adjudicated-invalid`, does not spawn a second adjudicator, and does not open a new full pass on unchanged code to get a different opinion.

evals.prompt: Loop-review my last commit (already on HEAD) in src/api/. You initialised with --base HEAD~1 and the reviewer came back saying it found nothing to review because the working tree is clean.
evals.expected_output: Recognises that the reviewer was never told the base: with --base the worktree is clean and `git diff HEAD` is empty, so the prompt's "Compare against" line must carry the base ref from `status`. Re-sends the corrected prompt to the same reviewer rather than recording an empty review, and does not treat "nothing to review" as zero findings.

evals.prompt: Loop-review src/worker/. The reviewer's section C discusses the tests in prose but never says trusted, justified-absent or inadequate.
evals.expected_output: Records the pass with what the reviewer actually gave (`pass-record --findings N --understood`, no `--test-evidence`), asks the same reviewer once for the missing verdict word, then `amend --test-evidence ...` against that same pass. Does not infer the category from the reviewer's prose, does not supply it itself, and does not open a new pass.

evals.prompt: Loop-review src/ui/. Your validation command is `npm run format && npm test` and the formatter rewrites two of the scoped files.
evals.expected_output: Notices the script recorded the run as having moved the scope and refusing to count it as evidence, then re-runs the checks on the now-settled files instead of forcing the pass open. Does not use `pass-start --force` and does not treat the first green run as validation of the reviewed state.

evals.prompt: Run a full project review. The session was interrupted halfway; `project status` shows one area still in_progress and its loop state is gone.
evals.expected_output: Runs `project close --force` to record that area incomplete and continues the queue from the next pending area — the one --force the workflow expects the agent to use on its own. Does not reset the project, does not re-queue completed areas, and does not stop the whole review on the stuck one.

evals.prompt: Review the whole repository area by area. One of the area paths you passed was a typo and matches no files.
evals.expected_output: Hits `project init` refusing the queue with exit 2 and naming every path that matches no file, corrects them, and re-queues before any area is opened. If a path only breaks later, `project next` records that area `incomplete` and the agent runs `project next` again for the one behind it. Never passes --allow-empty, and never `project init --force` on a queue whose areas already have outcomes, which would discard them.

evals.prompt: Loop-review src/checkout/. While the reviewer was reading, I saved two of those files in my editor.
evals.expected_output: Recognises the review describes a state that no longer exists and discards it with `pass-abort --reason ...`, then re-validates and opens a fresh pass on the settled files. Does not record an invented score/findings/verdict for the discarded review, and does not `reset` the loop.

evals.prompt: Do a full report-only review of this repo. Heads up: the test suite has been failing on main for weeks and nobody has fixed it.
evals.expected_output: Records the failing check with `validate`, opens the report-only pass over it rather than treating it as a blocker or hunting for a command that passes, and writes the red checks into the area's findings file as findings about the area. Does not use `pass-start --force`, does not fix anything, and does not `validate-drop` a check that genuinely ran and failed.

evals.prompt: Report-only review of the whole repo. In one area the reviewer returned two vague paragraphs and, after you asked once, still no findings, no summary and no verdict.
evals.expected_output: Closes that area as `incomplete` with its blocker via a plain `project close` and continues to the next area — no `--force`, no invented score or verdict, no stopping the project. Reports the area's outcome and blocker in the final per-area ledger.

evals.prompt: Continue the project review from yesterday. One of the areas was a directory that has since been renamed.
evals.expected_output: Runs `project next`, sees the renamed area recorded `incomplete` with its blocker, and runs `project next` again to reach the areas behind it — it does not stop the project, and does not `project init --force`, which would rebuild the ledger and discard the outcomes already earned. Reports that area's blocker in the final ledger.

evals.prompt: Loop-review src/client.ts. The reviewer's finding says the real cause is in src/helper.ts, which is not in the scope you recorded.
evals.expected_output: Fixes helper.ts and widens the scope with `scope -- src/helper.ts` before finishing, so the fix moves the fingerprint and a reviewer actually sees it. Does not accept on the strength of the earlier pass, and does not re-run `init --force`, which would discard the pass history.

evals.prompt: Review the docs/ directory of this project as an area. There are no tests, no linter and no build for it.
evals.expected_output: Records `validate --none --reason "..."` and passes that reason to the reviewer verbatim in the validation section of the prompt. Does not run `validate -- true` to get past `pass-start`, and does not present the absence as a check that passed.
